# Appending to a page stored under the directory of its type

# A page is addressed either by the path it is stored at or by its bare
# filename, which resolves under the directory of its type. Both append paths
# accept either form, and a page that is nowhere keeps the not-found report of
# the command that ran.

exec akb init type-dir-kb
cd type-dir-kb

stdin ../note-input.md
exec akb write type-dir-note.md
stdout 'Written to kb/notes/type-dir-note.md'

# akb append resolves the bare filename through the type directory
stdin ../first-appendix.txt
exec akb append type-dir-note.md
stdout 'Appended to kb/notes/type-dir-note.md'

# akb write --append resolves it the same way
stdin ../second-appendix.txt
exec akb write --append type-dir-note.md
stdout 'Appended to kb/notes/type-dir-note.md'

exec akb read notes/type-dir-note.md
stdout 'First appended line.'
stdout 'Second appended line.'

# The page was addressed by its bare filename and stays where it was
exists kb/notes/type-dir-note.md
! exists kb/type-dir-note.md

# An absent page keeps each command's own not-found report
stdin ../first-appendix.txt
! exec akb append absent-note.md
stderr 'page not found: absent-note.md. Use .akb write. to create'

stdin ../first-appendix.txt
! exec akb write --append absent-note.md
stderr 'page does not exist; use .akb write. without --append to create'

! exists kb/notes/absent-note.md
! exists kb/absent-note.md

-- note-input.md --
---
type: note
title: Bare Name Note
summary: Note addressed by its bare filename
tags: test
---
Bare name note body.

-- first-appendix.txt --
First appended line.

-- second-appendix.txt --
Second appended line.
